summary: This best current practice pins down what the acronym OAM means in IETF documents: Operations, Administration, and Maintenance. People had used it loosely and inconsistently, so the document defines the term and its component parts for use in all future IETF work.

eli5.summary: Lots of grown-ups use the same three-letter word to mean slightly different things. This paper says what the word means, like a class agreeing on one dictionary definition, so everyone talks about the same thing.

questions: what is the difference between oam and o&m
what does mgmt mean in rfcs
subtitle: The IETF settles on one meaning for OAM: Operations, Administration, and Maintenance.

tldr.problem: The acronym OAM is used everywhere in networking, but other standards bodies and even IETF documents expand it in different ways, which risks confusion and mistaken specifications.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC surveys existing uses, explains what each of the three letters covers, and recommends one expansion for all future IETF documents, plus O&M and Mgmt for related terms.
tldr.outcome: OAM is to be read as Operations, Administration, and Maintenance. RFC 10014 later updated this document with guidance on qualifiers such as in-band and out-of-band.

today: RFC 6291 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 161). It has been updated by RFC 10014, which covers qualifiers such as in-band and out-of-band used with OAM.

sections.title: Why OAM Needs a Definition
sections.content:
The acronym OAM is used widely in the data and telecommunication industry, so one would expect it to be clearly defined. RFC 6291 points out that a closer look shows recurring problems. Each letter stands for an integrated piece of functionality, and the acronym as a whole means more than the sum of its parts.

The main purpose of the document is to give one definition of OAM (Operations, Administration, and Maintenance) for use in all future IETF documents that refer to it. It also fixes the spelling of two related terms: O&M (OAM and Management) and Mgmt (Management).
sections.eli5: If two friends use the same word for different things, they will argue by mistake. This paper makes sure everyone means the same thing.

sections.title: How Other Bodies Use OAM
sections.content:
Other standards development organizations (SDOs) already used the term before the IETF wrote this guidance. The RFC lists several meanings:

  • Operations And Maintenance: network management functions for fault indication, performance information and diagnosis. ITU-T I.610 for ATM uses this form.
  • Operations, Administration, and Maintenance: the same group of functions, with fault localization added. Clause 57 of IEEE 802.3-2008 and ITU-T Y.1731 use this form.
  • The Metro Ethernet Forum describes OAM as the tools and utilities to install, monitor and troubleshoot a network (MEF 17).

ITU-T M.3010 also defines an operations systems function as a function block that processes information about telecommunications management.
sections.eli5: Different clubs had already used the word in their own ways. The paper first lists what each club meant.

sections.title: The Three Letters: O, A and M
sections.content:
The "O" invariably stands for Operations, although the scope of the term is somewhat ambivalent. Examples are performance monitoring tools used for service level agreement (SLA) measurement, fault management tools that watch the health of nodes and links, and network provisioning tools.

The "A" stands for Administration. Examples are network discovery and planning tools.

The "M" stands for Maintenance or Management. Examples of maintenance tools are connectivity check, loopback and link trace. ITU-T M.20 defines maintenance as the whole of operations required for setting up and maintaining any element involved in setting up a connection. A major aim of maintenance is to minimize both the occurrence and the impact of failures.
sections.eli5: O is for keeping things running, A is for keeping the lists, and M is for fixing and looking after things.

sections.title: Uses of OAM in the IETF
sections.content:
The IETF itself was not consistent. The RFC gives examples of how earlier RFCs expand the acronym, and notes the list is not exhaustive:

  • RFC 5586: Operations, Administration, and Maintenance.
  • RFC 3429: Operations and Maintenance.
  • RFC 4377: Operations and Management.
  • RFC 1812 writes O&M as OAM and Maintenance.

Sometimes a fourth letter is added: RFC 4594 uses OAM&P for Operations, Administration, Maintenance and Provisioning.
sections.eli5: Even the IETF's own papers did not agree, so the paper shows a few different spellings that were in use.

sections.title: The Recommended Usage
sections.content:
The IETF-recommended expansions are OAM for Operations, Administration, and Maintenance, O&M for OAM and Management, and Mgmt for Management.

  • Operations keeps the network and its services up and running. It includes monitoring and finding problems, ideally before users are affected.
  • Administration keeps track of resources in the network and how they are used, including the bookkeeping.
  • Maintenance facilitates repairs and upgrades, such as replacing equipment or patching a router, and includes corrective and preventive measures such as adjusting device configuration.

Provisioning, meaning configuring resources to support offered services, is outside the scope but is defined for completeness. In general, provisioning configures the network for new services, while OAM keeps the network able to support existing ones.

To talk about the combination of OAM and Management, spelling it out as "OAM and Management" is preferred. Where an acronym is needed, O&M should be used. Mgmt is used when an abbreviation for Management is needed. The document does not define Management.
sections.eli5: The paper says OAM means running things, keeping records, and fixing things. Setting up something brand new is a different job called provisioning.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document gives guidance on using an acronym and has no direct security implications. It does argue for an indirect benefit: a misunderstood acronym may lead to incorrect specification or implementation, which could open security problems in protocols or deployed networks. Clarifying the meaning of OAM therefore helps the future stability of specifications.
sections.eli5: If people misunderstand a word, they can build things wrongly, and wrongly built things can be unsafe. Agreeing on the word helps prevent that.
